# Living review protocol: Climate-related disclosure effectiveness map

```
Template version: 0.2
Title:                What makes climate-related disclosure requirements effective? A living map of
                      outcomes, mechanisms and factors
Protocol version:     0.9
Status:               draft (illustrative case study)
Last updated:         2026-11-24
```

> Illustrative case study. It is grounded in the IFRS Fellows concept note (Bolton, Ma, Leuz,
> Pereira da Silva & Reichlin, June 2025; `REF-0001`) as the seed reference. The prompts are in the
> template; only the responses appear here.

---

## S1. Scope

### S1.1 Purpose and users
- **Decision:** what criteria should be used to judge whether climate-related disclosure standards are
  succeeding? These criteria feed post-implementation reviews and national adoption choices. The seed
  note argues the criteria should be broader than how widely and how fast standards are adopted
  (REF-0001, p.14).
- **Research question:** which effects of disclosure requirements are well evidenced, which are only
  expected, and which matter but are unstudied?
- **Users:** standard-setter staff and trustees preparing evaluation criteria; regulators in
  jurisdictions adopting ISSB-based standards; researchers choosing studies.
- **Useful if:** a user can see, for any intended outcome, which mechanisms and factors are
  evidenced, how strongly, and where in the world.
- **Not useful if:** it collapses this into an overall "disclosure works / does not work" verdict.

### S1.2 Focus
Map the outcomes, mechanisms and factors related to the effectiveness of mandatory climate-related
corporate disclosure requirements, across jurisdictions. "Effectiveness" is always judged against a
specific intended outcome (registry column `intended_by`).

### S1.3 Element space
- **Outcome:** a change in firms, investors, markets or wider society that a reference attributes, or
  expects, to disclosure requirements. Example: O-02 lower cost of capital. This includes costs and
  harms.
- **Mechanism:** a behavioural or market process linking a requirement to an outcome. Example: M-04
  peer benchmarking.
- **Factor:** a requirement's design feature, or a firm, market or institutional condition, that
  changes whether or how much a mechanism operates. Example: F-02 enforcement and assurance.
- **Level of detail:** coarse. One element per distinct process or condition named in the seed note.
  Finer distinctions are out of scope for this review.
- **Seeds:** taken from REF-0001 §1–3 (see registry, S3.2). New elements may emerge during coding.

### S1.4 Boundaries
| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| Voluntary frameworks studied only as voluntary (no mandate or standard involved) | Not the policy instrument in focus. They are included when used as a comparison for mandates (selection is a known threat to these comparisons, REF-0001 p.7) |
| Effects of climate *risk* on prices without any disclosure element | Pricing literature, not disclosure (seed note appendix) |
| Product-level labels (e.g. energy labels) | Different actors and mechanisms; could be a later analogue review |
| Non-English references | Capacity. Recorded as a limitation in S4.5 |

Included, although a user might not expect it: **financial-reporting standard evidence (e.g. IFRS
adoption)**. The seed note relies on it heavily. It is tagged as analogue evidence (S3.4 relevance).

### S1.5 Review questions
- **Q1** Which outcomes are intended by in-scope requirements, and by whom? *(outcomes)*
- **Q2** For each intended outcome, which mechanisms are proposed and which are evidenced? *(outcomes × mechanisms)*
- **Q3** Which factors are reported to strengthen, weaken or block each mechanism? *(mechanisms × factors)*
- **Q4** Which unintended outcomes are reported or expected, through which mechanisms, and under which factors? *(all)*
- **Q5** Where is evidence absent, weak or confined to a few contexts? Prioritise by relevance to the S1.1 decision. *(all)*

---

## S2. Search

### S2.1 Sources
- **Seed and backward citation:** REF-0001; review articles cited in it (Leuz & Wysocki 2016;
  Christensen, Hail & Leuz 2021; Roychowdhury et al. 2019).
- **Academic databases:** OpenAlex, SSRN and RePEc, for working papers. The literature is
  working-paper heavy.
- **Standard-setter documents:** ISSB/IFRS Basis for Conclusions, post-implementation review (PIR)
  agenda papers, and literature reviews by standard-setter staff.
- **Forward citation:** of included references with evidence type CE.
- **Not searched (this version):** consultation comment letters and news. These are high-volume
  sources whose value is unknown; they are candidates for a later change.

**Added for Q1 (amended, see change log):**
- policy-development documents for policies in the policy list: legislative proposals, impact assessments, consultation papers, standard-setters' Bases for Conclusions, final rules and adopting releases;
- reports by international bodies on climate-disclosure policy (e.g. UN entities, FSB/TCFD, IOSCO, NGFS).

Found through the issuing bodies' websites and web search, and logged as usual.

### S2.2 Search procedure and log
- **OpenAlex** (title/abstract):
  `(climate OR carbon OR "greenhouse gas" OR GHG OR sustainability OR ESG OR CSR) AND (disclos* OR reporting) AND (mandat* OR regulat* OR standard* OR requirement*)`, 2000–present.
- **SSRN / RePEc:** the same terms in their own query syntax. The exact strings are kept in `search/queries.md`.
- **Citation chasing:** one round backward and one round forward from the included CE references.
- **Log (`search/log.csv`):** date, source, query or seed reference, number of results, number new after de-duplication.

### S2.3 Inclusion rules
| Rule | Passes | Fails |
|---|---|---|
| I1 Makes an empirical or theoretical claim about consequences of corporate disclosure or reporting requirements or standards | Study of emissions after the UK 2013 mandate | Survey of which ESG frameworks firms use, with no consequences studied |
| I2 The requirement concerns climate or sustainability information, **or** it is a financial-reporting requirement used as an analogue | IFRS adoption and market liquidity | Study of bank capital rules |
| I3 Full text available | SSRN working paper | Paywalled with no accessible version (log it as "unretrievable") |
| I4 (amended) Policy-development document or international-body report that states objectives or intended outcomes of an in-scope requirement. Included for Q1 only | The CSRD legislative proposal's statement of objectives | A press release announcing adoption without stating objectives |

Borderline cases go to the decision log. Example: ESG-rating studies where the rating is driven by disclosure.

### S2.4 Screening procedure
- **Stages:** title/abstract, then full text, each applying I1–I3.
- **Double screening:** the first 200 title/abstract decisions and 20% of full texts are screened
  independently twice. Report percentage agreement and Cohen's κ.
- **Disagreements:** resolved by discussion; each resolution is logged.
- **Record per reference:** decision, rule that failed (if excluded), screener, date.

### S2.5 Updating
- **Schedule:** re-run S2.2 quarterly.
- **Event triggers:** a new mandate is adopted or rolled back, or a PIR paper is published.
- **New references:** screened under the current protocol version.
- **Earlier decisions:** kept as they are. A rule change that would alter them is handled under S5.2.

---

## S3. Coding and appraisal

### S3.1 Unit of coding
- **One record = one claim** relating at least one element to another, anchored to one passage.
- **Several findings in one reference:** one record each.
- **The same finding in several references:**
  - code it from the most primary reference available;
  - other references get a record that points to it through `same_as` and is not counted twice in synthesis.
- **Second-hand reports** (common in a seed note):
  - code the finding from the secondary reference, with `primary_source` filled in;
  - flag the primary for retrieval;
  - once the primary is coded, set `superseded_by` on the secondary record.
- **Summary claims in reviews** ("evidence suggests reductions of 8–15%") are not coded as records,
  because they would double-count. The studies they summarise are added as search seeds.
- **Missing element roles:** a record that relates a factor to an outcome without stating a mechanism
  leaves the mechanism empty and is flagged `mechanism_unstated`. These records feed the Q2 gaps.
- **Statements that evidence is lacking** ("not much research has been done…") become records with
  evidence type `ABS`.

### S3.2 Element registry (seeds from REF-0001)
Review-specific column: `intended_by`, the instrument or actor that states this outcome as an
objective, with a source. It is filled only from coded sources (Q1), never assumed; "to code" means
not yet established. Blank means no source states it as intended.

| ID | Name | Definition | Broader | intended_by | Status | added_in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O-01 | Market liquidity | Lower trading frictions from reduced information asymmetry among investors | — | to code (Q1) | active | v0.1 |
| O-02 | Firm cost of capital | Required return on a firm's equity or debt | — | to code (Q1) | active | v0.1 |
| O-03 | Firm GHG emissions | Emissions of firms subject to requirements | — | to code (Q1) | active | v0.1 |
| O-04 | Reporting quality & comparability | Informativeness and cross-firm comparability of what is reported | — | IFRS Foundation: "decision usefulness of information" (REF-0001 p.14) | active | v0.1 |
| O-05 | Compliance cost | Direct cost of measuring and reporting | — | — | active | v0.1 |
| O-06 | Innovation / investment | Firms' investment and innovation activity | — | — | active | v0.1 |
| O-07 | Green capital reallocation | Shift of capital toward lower-carbon firms or projects | — | to code (Q1) | active | v0.1 |
| M-01 | Information-asymmetry reduction | Public information narrows information gaps between investors | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-02 | Comparability spillovers | Standardised information lowers the cost of processing information about *other* firms | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-03 | Outside monitoring | Investors and analysts discipline managerial decisions | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-04 | Peer benchmarking | Firms learn their relative performance from peers' disclosures | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-05 | Internal measurement | Being required to measure creates information inside the firm itself | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-06 | Proprietary-cost exposure | Disclosure reveals commercially sensitive information to competitors | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-07 | Avoidance / boilerplate | Firms for which costs exceed benefits comply in form only | — | | active | v0.1 |
| M-08 | Investor engagement & divestment | Responsible investors engage with firms or exit them | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-01 | Mandatory vs voluntary regime | Whether disclosure is required | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-02 | Enforcement & assurance | Supervision, sanctions and external assurance of reports | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-03 | Firm reporting incentives | A firm's own costs and benefits of informative reporting | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-04 | Firm size | Scale; determines fixed-cost burden | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-05 | Sector carbon intensity | Emissions intensity of the firm's sector | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-06 | Materiality basis | Financial vs double materiality | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-07 | Standard discretion | Choices left to firms (e.g. GHG Protocol boundaries, Scope 3 estimation) | — | | active | v0.1 |
| F-08 | Institutional quality | Legal system, regulatory capacity; developed vs developing economy | — | | active | v0.1 |

- **Add:** any coder may propose an element in the decision log. The review lead approves it and
  assigns the next ID.
- **Merge / split:** requires a change-log entry if the element appears in more than 5 records;
  otherwise the decision log is enough.

### S3.3 Coding schema
Core fields as in the template, plus:

| Field | Definition / values |
|---|---|
| `primary_source` | citation of the original study, if the record is second-hand |
| `same_as` / `superseded_by` | record IDs (S3.1) |
| `instrument` | named requirement, e.g. "UK Companies Act 2013 GHG reporting", "IFRS adoption (analogue)" |
| `direction` | `+` / `−` / `none` / `conditional` / `unclear`: effect on the outcome as the passage states it |
| `text_accessed` | `full_text` / `abstract` / `second_hand` (coded from another reference's report) |

Example record:
```
record_id:      REC-001
reference_id:   REF-0001 (Bolton et al. 2025)
passage:        "facilities reduce emissions by roughly 8% once forced to disclosure" (p.11)
primary_source: Tomar (2023), J. Accounting Research 61(2)
elements:       F-01 factor; M-04 mechanism; O-03 outcome
relationship:   Mandatory facility-level GHG reporting (US GHGRP) reduced facility emissions ~8%,
                with evidence consistent with peer benchmarking as the mechanism.
direction:      −  (on emissions)
context:        US manufacturing facilities, from 2010
instrument:     US EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program
evidence_type:  CE
appraisal:      strength = provisional (second-hand; recode from primary); relevance = Direct
protocol_version: 0.2      coded_by: AH   checked_by: —
```

**Mechanism status (amended, see change log).** Each mechanism in `elements` carries `status`:
- `tested`: the reference reports evidence that bears specifically on this mechanism (e.g. a test of the channel, heterogeneity designed to isolate it, or a measured mediator);
- `proposed`: the reference offers it as an explanation, interpretation or hypothesis, without such evidence.

A record whose mechanisms are all `proposed` keeps its evidence type for the factor–outcome link, but the mechanism itself does not count as evidenced.

**Policy, place and time (amended, see change log).** Every record also carries:

| Field | Definition / values |
|---|---|
| `policies` | IDs from the policy list below (empty if no specific policy) |
| `jurisdictions` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, or `EU`, `multi` (list them in `context`) or `global` |
| `period` | `{start, end}`: years of the data or events studied. For a policy document, the year of the document |
| `evidence_year` | the year the finding first became public: the earliest known version of the primary study, or the year of a policy document |

**Policy list.** This table sits beside the element registry. Columns:
- `P-nn` ID;
- name;
- jurisdiction;
- type (`mandate` / `standard` / `voluntary framework` / `proposal`);
- key dates (proposed, adopted, effective, amended, withdrawn), each with a source;
- notes.

Entries are added and approved like elements (S3.2).

### S3.4 Appraisal
**Evidence type:**
- `CE`: causal estimate from a design that compares against a counterfactual;
- `AS`: association;
- `DE`: description of practice or prevalence;
- `TH`: theory or formal model;
- `EX`: expectation or conjecture by experts or stakeholders;
- `ABS`: a statement that evidence is lacking.

**Strength** (CE and AS only):

| Level | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| High | CE whose design addresses both selection into disclosure and concurrent reforms | Treated vs already-voluntary disclosers around one mandate date, with no reported concurrent reform |
| Medium | CE with one of those threats unaddressed, or a strong AS | IFRS liquidity study before controlling for enforcement changes |
| Low | AS with obvious selection; or CE the reference itself says it cannot attribute | Voluntary disclosers have 21% lower emissions the following year (REF-0001 p.10) |
| provisional | Second-hand or abstract-only record, not yet checked against the primary full text | REC-001 |

**Relevance:**
- `Direct`: a climate or sustainability mandate, in the context named in the question.
- `Indirect`: an analogue instrument (financial reporting), voluntary regimes used as comparison, or a different context.
- `Remote`: an analogy across sectors or policy types.

**Added evidence type (amended, see change log):** `INT` = a statement of intended outcome by a policymaker, standard-setter or international body. It is used for Q1 and to fill `intended_by`. It is never used as evidence that the outcome occurs, and has no strength rating.

### S3.5 Coding procedure and consistency
- **Coders:** one coder codes each reference; a second coder independently codes 20% of references,
  sampled at random each quarter.
- **Agreement:**
  - element assignment: overlap (Jaccard) of the element sets;
  - evidence type, strength and relevance: κ.
- **Disagreements:** resolved by discussion and logged.
- **Ambiguities logged:**
  - an element that doesn't fit any definition;
  - a passage with more than one plausible `relationship` reading;
  - any `direction = unclear`.

### S3.6 Worked examples
| Case | Record | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| CE, second-hand | REC-001 above | `primary_source`; provisional strength |
| Analogue CE with a factor | REC-002: liquidity effects around IFRS adoption are concentrated in five EU countries that changed enforcement at the same time (REF-0001 p.5; Christensen, Hail & Leuz 2013). Elements: F-02, M-01, O-01. `direction = conditional`, relevance Indirect | Analogue evidence; conditional effect |
| AS with selection | REC-003: voluntary disclosers have lower emissions the following year, "most likely" reflecting selection (p.10; Aldy et al. 2023). Elements: F-01, O-03. AS, strength Low | Weak evidence is kept and graded, not dropped |
| ABS + EX (hard case) | REC-004: little research on reporting costs. Costs are expected to scale with firm size (economies of scale) (p.8). Elements: F-04, O-05. One passage gives two records: `ABS` (costs) and `EX` (scaling) | One passage → two records; absence of evidence becomes a record |
| TH | REC-005: standardisation creates information externalities that firms do not internalise, so voluntary disclosure gives too little comparability (p.2; Admati & Pfleiderer 2000). Elements: F-01, M-02, O-04. TH | Theory records feed Q2, not confidence |
| Unintended outcome | REC-006: proprietary costs of mandated disclosure can reduce incentives to innovate, invest or list (p.6; Breuer, Leuz & Vanhaverbeke 2025). Elements: F-01, M-06, O-06. `direction = −`, CE, provisional | Unintended outcome coded with the same schema as intended ones |

---

## S4. Synthesis

### S4.1 Outputs
1. **Element map:** an outcome × factor matrix, with mechanisms listed in each cell. Each cell shows
   its record count by evidence type. Answers Q2–Q4.
2. **Summary per outcome:** for each O element, the statements with their confidence, its `intended_by`
   and any conflicts. Answers Q1, Q2, Q4.
3. **Gap list:** answers Q5.

All three are kept as plain tables (`synthesis/vN/`).

### S4.2 From records to statements
- **Grouping:** by outcome, then mechanism, then factor. One statement per outcome–mechanism pair,
  noting the factors that change it.
- **Conflicting records:** if `context` explains the conflict, write a conditional statement
  ("… only where F-02 is strong"). If it doesn't, the statement is labelled *inconsistent* and both
  sets of records are cited.
- **Citing:** every statement lists its record IDs. Records marked `same_as` or `superseded_by` are not
  counted.

### S4.3 Confidence
| Level | Rule |
|---|---|
| High | ≥2 independent records with High strength and Direct relevance, agreeing, with no unexplained conflict |
| Moderate | ≥1 High, or ≥2 Medium, record with Direct or Indirect relevance, agreeing |
| Low | Only Low or provisional records, or only Indirect/Remote relevance |
| Expected only | Only TH/EX records; labelled as such and never merged with empirical statements |

### S4.4 Gaps
**Gap types:**
- (a) an intended outcome with no CE/AS records;
- (b) a mechanism with only TH/EX records;
- (c) an outcome × factor cell with no records in a context in scope (e.g. developing economies, smaller firms);
- (d) any ABS record.

**Priority:** first, gaps bearing on intended outcomes (Q1), since evaluation criteria need these; then
by the number of in-scope jurisdictions affected.

**Added gap type (e) (amended, see change log):** *untested mechanism*. A mechanism whose records all have `status = proposed`.

### S4.5 Interpretation and limits
- **Form:** statements describe the conditions under which outcomes are and are not observed.
- **Not made:** no policy recommendations, and no overall verdict on effectiveness.
- **Standing limitations:**
  - English only;
  - seed-note framing may steer the element set;
  - heavy reliance on second-hand records in early versions;
  - consultation and practitioner evidence not yet searched.

### S4.6 Versions of the synthesis
- **When:** a new version is released quarterly, if any statement or gap changes.
- **Change table:** statements added, revised or retired, each with its cause: new records, recoding,
  or a change ID.

**Synthesis history (amended, see change log).** Every statement and gap keeps a `history`: its records ordered by `evidence_year`. For each record:
- `effect`: one of `establishes` / `corroborates` / `extends` (new context) / `qualifies` (adds a condition) / `contradicts` / `weakens` / `signals_gap`;
- a one-sentence blurb on how the record changed the statement relative to earlier records.

The synthesis from the previous release is kept, so changes between releases can be shown.

---

## S5. Maintenance

### S5.1 Decision log
`logs/decisions.csv` with the template's minimum fields. It is reviewed at each synthesis release;
any ambiguity logged three or more times triggers a proposed change.

Example entry:
```
2026-11-24 | S3.1 | REF-0001 p.8 | "Not much research has been done on costs" coded as a record
           | No evidence type fits statements of absence; needed for gap type (d) | AH
```

### S5.2 Change log
| Change ID | Date | Item ID | Change (before → after) | Reason | Effect on existing records | Version after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CH-001 | 2026-11-24 | S3.4 | Evidence types CE/AS/DE/TH/EX → add `ABS` | Decision-log entry above; gap type (d) needs it | Recode pilot records containing statements of absence (2 records) | 0.2 |
| CH-002 | 2026-11-24 | S2.1 | Sources → add policy-development documents and international-body reports | Q1 could not be answered: `intended_by` was "to code" for 6 of 10 outcomes after the pilot; user request | none (new search) | 0.3 |
| CH-003 | 2026-11-24 | S2.3 | Rules I1–I3 → add I4: documents stating intended outcomes are included for Q1 | I1 required claims about consequences, which excluded statements of objectives | none | 0.4 |
| CH-004 | 2026-11-24 | S3.4 | Evidence types → add `INT` (statement of intended outcome) | Statements of intent needed a type that cannot be mistaken for evidence of effects | none | 0.5 |
| CH-005 | 2026-11-24 | S3.3 | Mechanism entries have no status → each mechanism carries `status`: tested / proposed | Pilot: Q2 asks which mechanisms are proposed vs evidenced, but the schema could not record it (run notes and decision log); user request | recode all records | 0.6 |
| CH-006 | 2026-11-24 | S3.3 | No structured policy/place/time → add `policies`, `jurisdictions`, `period`, `evidence_year`, plus a policy list | Context was free text, so records could not be related to specific policies, countries or periods; user request | recode all records | 0.7 |
| CH-007 | 2026-11-24 | S4.4 | Gap types → add (e) untested mechanism | Follows from the mechanism-status change; pilot found mechanisms supported only by explanations | none (regenerate gaps) | 0.8 |
| CH-008 | 2026-11-24 | S4.6 | No per-statement provenance over time → statements and gaps keep a `history` of records with effect and blurb | Needed to show how the synthesis built up over time; user request | none (regenerate synthesis) | 0.9 |

review.title: Do disclosure mandates reduce firm emissions — really? Mechanisms and factors
review.focus: Map the mechanisms and factors underlying firms' greenhouse-gas emissions when emissions disclosure is required, separating reductions in reported emissions from real ones.

questions.text: Do disclosure mandates reduce O-02, by how much, and in which contexts?
Which mechanisms are evidenced rather than only proposed?
Do reductions in O-02 correspond to reductions in O-03, or do firms redraw their boundaries?
Which factors (enforcement, sector, rule-design features F-04 to F-08) change Q1–Q3?
Where is evidence missing? Prioritise by relevance to the S1.1 design decisions.

registry.name: Firm GHG emissions

registry.definition: Operating performance of covered firms

registry.definition: Firms learn their relative performance from peers' disclosures

registry.definition: Being required to measure creates information inside the firm

registry.definition: Firms move emitting assets outside the reporting boundary (sale, outsourcing, relocation)

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: Emissions-disclosure mandates were followed by reductions of about 7–8% in facility- or installation-level measured emissions in two settings: US GHGRP industrial facilities, and EU ETS installations of UK-listed firms after the 2013 UK rule. A third, abstract-only estimate for the UK rule is larger (about 16%). decision_log.reason: Rule gap (CH-P02).

decision_log.decision: Conflict resolved as conditional on measure (facility-measured vs firm-level provider data with estimated controls), not labelled inconsistent.
decision_log.reason: S4.2: context explains the conflict.

decision_log.decision: Emission rates/intensity and absolute levels are both coded as O-02.
decision_log.reason: O-02 does not separate intensity from level. Bauckloh et al. show they can diverge in sign (CH-P07).

decision_log.decision: Second-hand REF-0001 records kept and marked superseded_by the primary records, to show the trail. REF-0001 second-hand records for Jouvenot & Krueger and Aldy et al. not created because primary text was coded directly.
decision_log.reason: S3.1 rule; avoids double counting in synthesis.

decision_log.decision: M-02 status = proposed, although REF-0001 p.11 says De Bettignies et al. 'show' that required measurement disciplines CSR.
decision_log.reason: Re-checked the primary (NBER w28159 rev0, Dec 2020): the closest analyses (a within-UK CDP comparison and environmental vs other sub-scores) are framed as oversight intensity and do not isolate measurement or private signals. The seed note's 'show' overstates this. REC-003 (superseded) follows the primary.

decision_log.decision: M-03 status = proposed.
decision_log.reason: Abstract-only. The abstract says the authors 'present evidence consistent with' higher future costs of emissions and easier cross-firm comparisons, but the tests are not visible, and the M-03 mapping of 'financial motivations' is itself an interpretation. Per ITER2_SPEC, 'proposed' is used when unsure. Note: 'facilitated across firm comparisons' may correspond to M-01. The record is not recoded until the full text is read.

decision_log.decision: M-03 status = tested, although the key public-ownership triple interaction is not significant.
decision_log.reason: 'Tested' means that evidence bears specifically on the mechanism, not that the evidence supports it. Yang et al. design ownership-type and S&P 500 heterogeneity explicitly as a shareholder-pressure test (p.21). The weak result is carried in ST-08 text and confidence.

decision_log.decision: M-03 status = tested.
decision_log.reason: RepRisk environmental incidents (public scrutiny) are measured and used as the explanatory variable that predicts divestment (Dec 2022 version, Section 5.2). Here M-03 operates under non-disclosure pressure (Indirect), so it does not count as M-03 evidence for disclosure mandates (G-06).

decision_log.decision: Status = tested for null results (relocation abroad M-05; measurement alone M-02).
decision_log.reason: Both are designed to isolate the channel: industry geographic mobility, and the 2010-11 measured-but-not-public window. A null test is still a test.

decision_log.decision: M-05 status = proposed in an ABS record.
decision_log.reason: The source raises leakage as an untested possibility; no evidence bears on it.

decision_log.decision: jurisdictions lists the jurisdiction(s) of the treated units or the policy studied; control-group countries (e.g. Canada for REF-0002, EU15 for REF-0004/REF-0005) are left in context. REF-0009's worldwide listed firms are coded US because treatment is ownership of US GHGRP facilities. REF-0012's foreign suppliers are coded US (the firms studied).
decision_log.reason: S3.3 does not say whether control jurisdictions count. Listing them would make the field useless for 'which policy contexts are evidenced'.

decision_log.decision: period: second-hand records take the primary study's sample years; REF-0001's own statements, theory and conceptual records take the document year (start = end).
decision_log.reason: S3.3 defines document year only for policy documents. Theory has no data period, and the closest analogue is the document version that states it.

decision_log.decision: evidence_year rule: the year of the first public version of the primary study (working paper counts), unless a checked earlier version shows the specific finding absent or different. In that case the year is the earliest version known to contain it. The basis is recorded in extra.evidence_year_basis.
decision_log.reason: S3.3 defines evidence_year per finding ('the year the finding first became public'), but for most studies only the first posting date could be verified, not each finding's presence in it.

DIW DP 1795 (Aug 2019; author list includes Rettenbacher instead of Reichelstein, and the title differs) is treated as an earlier version because DIW lists DP 1875 as an updated version of DP 1795. DP 1795 reports reductions vs listed EU15 firms (~15-18%, not ~8%) that 'appear to be permanent'. It contradicts REC-017's convergence finding, and its abstract does not address financial performance.

decision_log.reason: The WP abstract says absolute emissions 'did not change', which differs from the published 'reduced significantly less than control firms'. The year is the same either way. Records are not recoded; the WP-vs-published difference is noted in ST-04 conditions.

decision_log.decision: Q2 statements carry a 'mechanism_status' object listing tested and proposed records. Only tested records count as mechanism evidence. ST-10 gains REC-014 (tested null). Type (f) is applied to M-06 (G-09, overlapping G-03 type b) and to M-04 (G-10, no records at all).

S2.1/S2.2 OpenAlex, SSRN and RePEc database queries were not run as specified. Instead: two web searches with simplified forms of S2.2 query 2 (SL-10, SL-11). S2.2 query 1 was not run.

Six seed-list references (investor/SRI theory: Heinkel et al.; Broccardo et al.; Chowdhry et al.; Oehmke & Opp; Becht, Franks et al.; plus reviews Christensen, Hail & Leuz 2018/2021) were DEFERRED without full screening. The output schema has no 'deferred' value, so they are recorded as 'excluded' with reason text starting 'DEFERRED' or stating 'not accessed'. S2.1 review-chasing of Christensen et al. (2021) was not done.

Verbatim passages from non-seed references were obtained through the WebFetch tool, whose extraction model returns quoted excerpts. They were not checked character-by-character against the PDFs by a human. Seed-note passages were string-matched against the local text file.

Several references were read in working-paper versions rather than the published version: Tomar (ECGI WP), Duchin et al. (Dec/Mar 2022 WPs), Yang et al. (NBER WP via an SEC comment-file copy), Comello et al. (accepted manuscript), Aldy et al. (April 2023 WP). Page locators refer to those versions.

reviews.run_notes: Iteration 2 (protocol v0.5): all 40 records recoded for CH-001/CH-002 (mechanism status; policies, jurisdictions, period, evidence_year). Five policies created. Synthesis regenerated with histories (CH-004), Q2 statements now separate tested vs proposed mechanisms, and two type (f) gaps added (CH-003). Main findings from the recheck: Downar et al.'s 2019 version reported larger and 'permanent' UK reductions, which conflicts with the published transitory finding. De Bettignies et al. use 2011, not 2013, as the intervention year (REC-022 context fixed). No pilot change proposal (CH-P01..P08) is covered by the amendments; all remain open. || PILOT: Pilot run of protocol B v0.1 by a single agent. 12 references included (seed plus 6 seed-cited, 2 backward, 3 from searches), 55 screened references excluded or deferred, 40 records, 21 statements, 8 gaps. Key findings: facility-measured reductions of about 7-8% under the US GHGRP and the UK 2013 rule (High, per S4.3 literally). The UK effect looks transitory. The only Direct test of reported vs real (Yang et al., US power) finds covered-plant cuts offset by shifting to below-threshold plants (Moderate). Divestment, cross-state relocation and supplier outsourcing evidence is Indirect (Low). Main protocol problems: the measurement scale counts facility-level data as 'distinguishes' even though it cannot detect reallocation; S4.3 lacks rules for one Medium record, same-study records and DE/ABS; S4.4 lacks a gap type for under-evidenced rule-design factors; the emissions_measure and boundary value sets do not fit regulator inventories or portfolio boundaries; O-02 pools intensity and levels. Seed-note issues: REF-0001's 'Aldy et al. (2023)' findings are in a different Aldy et al. (2023) paper; its 8-15% range omits Jouvenot & Krueger's ~16% (revised abstract); two in-text citations are missing from its reference list.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: Emissions-disclosure mandates were followed by reductions of about 7–8% in facility- or installation-level measured emissions in two settings: US GHGRP industrial facilities, and EU ETS installations of UK-listed firms after the 2013 UK rule. A third, abstract-only estimate for the UK rule is larger (about 16%). REPORTED vs REAL: these are real reductions at the covered facilities, but none of these records tracks boundary-inclusive emissions (O-03). See ST-11 and ST-15. [Measurement: REC-008=distinguishes; REC-015=distinguishes; REC-020=unknown]
statements.confidence_reason: Two independent High/Direct CE records agree (Tomar; Downar), per S4.3 applied literally. The abstract-only record is provisional and agrees in direction.
statements.conditions: Covered facilities only. US manufacturing (GHGRP, from 2012) and UK-listed firms' European installations (energy sector excluded). Short horizon. High applies to facility-level reductions, not to firm-wide or boundary-inclusive emissions.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: In US power plants, GHGRP coverage reduced plant CO2 emission RATES by about 7%. This is consistent in sign with ST-01, but the outcome is an intensity, not a level. [Measurement: REC-027=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: A single Medium record. S4.3 has no level for one Medium record, so Low was assigned conservatively (decision log; CH-P02).
statements.conditions: US electric power sector 2004–2018. The control (below-threshold plants) is contaminated by within-firm shifting (REC-028).

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: The UK mandate's effect on installation emissions appears transitory: treated firms' emissions converge back to controls after about two years. [Measurement: REC-017=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: One High/Direct record (S4.3: ≥1 High).
statements.conditions: UK-listed firms' EU ETS installations, firm-level event study.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: With firm-level provider data (Trucost, partly estimated), GHGRP-affected firms improved carbon intensity but cut absolute Scope 1 emissions LESS than controls. This conflicts with ST-01 on levels. The difference in measure and the estimated control-group values plausibly explain the conflict. Not written as a claim about real emissions: all records are 'cannot'. [Measurement: REC-031=cannot; REC-032=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: Two Medium records from one study, on different outcome definitions (intensity vs level), so they do not 'agree' on one claim. Measurement 'cannot'.
statements.conditions: Listed firms worldwide; firm-level Trucost Scope 1; firm boundary not fixed.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: Voluntary emissions disclosers have about 21% lower next-year emissions than non-disclosers. The source attributes this to selection, so it is not evidence of a disclosure effect. [Measurement: REC-024=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: A single Low, Indirect AS record. Measurement 'cannot'.
statements.conditions: Russell 3000, 2011–2020; voluntary regime (F-01 = voluntary).

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: Peer benchmarking (M-01) is the only mechanism with direct causal support for a disclosure-induced reduction, and it comes from one study (US GHGRP). Second-hand report: REC-002 (superseded). [Measurement: REC-009=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: A single Medium record (no S4.3 level for one Medium; conservative Low). REC-002 is superseded and does not count as independent.
statements.conditions: US industrial facilities.

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: Internal measurement alone (M-02), without public disclosure, is not evidenced to reduce emissions. In the GHGRP's private-measurement years there was no significant response. In the UK, required measurement with an opt-out lowered report-based environmental CSR scores, with no emissions estimate. [Measurement: REC-010=distinguishes; REC-022=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: One Low/Direct CE record on emissions and one Medium/Remote record on a non-emissions outcome.
statements.conditions: US 2010–11 private-measurement period; UK 2013 regime.

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: Outside monitoring / investor pressure (M-03) is proposed by authors as a driver, but the evidence is inconsistent. UK authors conclude financial motivations drive reductions (abstract only). In US power plants, effects are larger for publicly traded owners, though the difference is not significant. For US industrial facilities, effects are larger for non-public owners and stock returns do not react. [Measurement: REC-021=unknown; REC-030=distinguishes; REC-012=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: Records point in different directions on listed vs non-listed owners. No context rule in the records resolves it, though sector (power vs manufacturing) is a candidate.
statements.conditions: Power plants (Yang et al.) vs manufacturing facilities (Tomar); UK listed firms (Jouvenot & Krueger).

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: Exemption use / avoidance (M-06) is supported only by theory and conjecture: low-CSR firms use a non-disclosure option, and high-cost firms comply in form only. Large reported reductions at facilities exiting the GHGRP are described but not attributed to any mechanism. [Measurement: REC-023=not applicable (theory); REC-006=unknown; REC-013=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: Only TH/EX records bear on M-06. REC-013 is DE with mechanism_unstated. S4.3 has no rule for DE (decision log).

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: Boundary redrawing (M-05) is evidenced: by within-firm shifting to below-threshold plants under a disclosure mandate (Direct), and by plant divestment, cross-state relocation and supplier outsourcing under other pressures (Indirect). [Measurement: REC-028=distinguishes; REC-033=distinguishes; REC-034=distinguishes; REC-037=distinguishes; REC-039=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: One Direct Medium CE (REC-028) plus several Indirect Medium records from independent studies, agreeing that M-05 operates. This rests on reading 'agreeing' as agreement that the mechanism occurs; the outcome-level claims are in ST-11 to ST-14.
statements.conditions: US power sector (Direct); US industrial plants, California cap-and-trade, US firms' foreign suppliers (Indirect).

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: REPORTED vs REAL (Direct): under the US GHGRP, power-sector firms owning plants on both sides of the reporting threshold raised emission rates at non-reporting plants. Their portfolio-wide emission rates did not change, so the reduction at covered plants (ST-02) did not carry over to boundary-inclusive emissions. [Measurement: REC-028=distinguishes; REC-029=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: Two Medium/Direct CE records agree, and both are 'distinguishes', which meets the O-03 added rule. Both come from one working paper, and S4.3 does not require independence for Moderate (CH-P02).
statements.conditions: US electric power, firms with plants above and below the 25,000 t threshold. Emission rates, not levels.

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: REPORTED vs REAL (Indirect): after environmental incidents, firms sell their most polluting plants to buyers under weaker scrutiny. Pollution at those plants does not decline while the sellers' ESG ratings improve. Toxic releases, not GHG. [Measurement: REC-033=distinguishes; REC-034=distinguishes; REC-035=distinguishes; REC-036=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: Only Indirect relevance (S4.3 Low rule), although REC-035 is 'distinguishes'.
statements.conditions: US TRI plants; no disclosure mandate; transfer to GHG under mandates is unverified.

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: REPORTED vs REAL (Indirect): under California cap-and-trade, financially constrained firms cut in-state emissions by moving emissions and output to plants in other states. Their firm-wide emissions rose. [Measurement: REC-037=distinguishes; REC-038=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: Only Indirect relevance (carbon pricing, no disclosure element).
statements.conditions: Regional carbon pricing; financially constrained firms only.

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: REPORTED vs REAL (Indirect): firms under environmental pressure reduce own-operation emissions by outsourcing to foreign suppliers. Totals including upstream Scope 3 do not fall. Not a claim about real emissions: records are 'cannot' (estimated Scope 3). [Measurement: REC-039=cannot; REC-040=cannot]
statements.confidence_reason: Indirect only, and no 'distinguishes' record (O-03 added rule caps at Low).
statements.conditions: US listed firms with foreign suppliers.

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: For the UK 2013 mandate and GHGRP manufacturing facilities, whether reported reductions (ST-01) correspond to boundary-inclusive reductions is untested. Leakage to non-European installations cannot be ruled out, and divested installations were excluded rather than followed. One indirect test finds US reductions concentrated in less geographically mobile industries. [Measurement: REC-018=not applicable (ABS: O-03 not measured); REC-014=distinguishes]
statements.confidence_reason: ABS record plus one Medium record coded on O-02 (indirect test). No O-03 record with 'distinguishes', so capped at Low by the added rule.
statements.conditions: UK-listed firms; US manufacturing.

statements.question: Q4
statements.text: Rule design (F-04/F-05/F-06): conceptual work argues that GHG Protocol direct-emissions accounting lets firms lower reported emissions by divestment or outsourcing, and that a cradle-to-gate (embodied-input) metric would remove that gain. Empirical evidence on consolidation-boundary choices is explicitly lacking. [Measurement: REC-025=not applicable (theory); REC-026=not applicable (theory); REC-004=unknown]
statements.confidence_reason: Only TH records plus one ABS.
statements.conditions: GHG Protocol-based regimes.

statements.question: Q4
statements.text: Exemption design (F-07): a size threshold for reporting enabled within-firm shifting to non-reporting plants (Direct, ST-11). Facilities exiting the GHGRP show large reported drops of unclear origin. Opt-out clauses are modelled to enable withholding of bad signals. [Measurement: REC-028=distinguishes; REC-013=distinguishes; REC-023=not applicable (theory)]
statements.confidence_reason: One Medium/Direct CE on F-07, plus DE and TH records. A single Medium record gives conservative Low.
statements.conditions: US GHGRP 25,000 t threshold; UK 'not practical' opt-out.

statements.question: Q4
statements.text: Firm conditions: reductions are smaller for organisationally complex firms (UK) and larger where legislation is anticipated (US). Financial constraints determine whether firms relocate emissions under regional carbon pricing (Indirect). [Measurement: REC-019=distinguishes; REC-011=distinguishes; REC-037=distinguishes]

gaps.text: No evidence on how GHG Protocol consolidation-boundary discretion (operational vs financial control, equity share) affects reported emissions or enables boundary redrawing (stated as under-researched in REF-0001).
gaps.priority_reason: Bears directly on F-05 (rule design), the first S1.1 decision.

gaps.text: Peer benchmarking (M-01) is evidenced for O-02 (Tomar) but never tested against O-03. Likewise the UK mandate effect (REC-015) has no O-03 test: non-European leakage and ownership-changed installations are not followed.
gaps.priority_reason: Central to Q3 and to whether boundary rules (F-05) are needed. The only Direct O-03 evidence (REC-028, REC-029) shows the reported-real wedge can be large.

gaps.text: Exemption use / avoidance (M-06) has only TH/EX records. No study measures how often the UK 'not practical' opt-out is invoked or what happens to emissions of firms using it. GHGRP exits are undiagnosed.
gaps.priority_reason: Bears on F-07 (exemption design).

gaps.text: No records on regimes that require Scope 3 (or embodied-emissions) reporting, so there is no evidence on whether Scope 3 coverage curbs outsourcing-based reductions (only theory, REC-026). Typed (c) as a context with no records; S4.4 has no type for a factor with only TH/EX (CH-P03).
gaps.priority_reason: Bears on F-06 (rule design).

gaps.text: No emissions-outcome records on assurance/enforcement intensity (F-02) for emissions disclosure, e.g. assured vs unassured reports or verified vs self-certified data.
gaps.priority_reason: Named in Q4. Not one of F-05 to F-07.

gaps.text: Outside monitoring / investor pressure (M-03) is proposed as a driver of O-02 reductions but never tested against O-03 under a disclosure mandate. Its only O-03-relevant evidence is Indirect (divestment after incidents, REC-033, REC-035).
gaps.priority_reason: Bears on F-08 (scrutiny gap) and Q3.

gaps.text: No records from emerging or developing economies, and none on ISSB S2, EU CSRD or other post-2020 mandates. The China CSR-mandate study (Chen et al. 2018) was excluded because its pollution measure is city-level.
gaps.priority_reason: Context gap; not directly a rule-design feature.

gaps.text: Long-run effects: the only durability evidence shows convergence after about two years (UK). No study covers more than about 5 post-mandate years.
gaps.priority_reason: Relevant to whether emissions reduction is a defensible success criterion (S1.1, 2nd decision).

reviews.protocol_md:
# Living review protocol: Disclosure mandates and real firm emissions

```
Template version: 0.2
Title:                Do disclosure mandates reduce firm emissions — really? Mechanisms and factors
Protocol version:     0.5
Status:               draft (illustrative case study)
Last updated:         2026-11-24
```

> Illustrative case study, outcome-focused. The seed reference is the IFRS Fellows concept note
> (Bolton, Ma, Leuz, Pereira da Silva & Reichlin, June 2025; `REF-0001`). Prompts are in the template.

---

## S1. Scope

### S1.1 Purpose and users
- **Decisions:**
  - Whether emissions-disclosure rules need design features that turn reductions in *reported*
    emissions into reductions in *real* emissions. Examples: consolidation-boundary rules, Scope 3
    coverage, limits on exemptions.
  - Whether emissions reduction is a defensible criterion for judging the success of climate
    disclosure standards.
- **Research question:** which mechanism produces the reported emissions reductions?
- **Users:** regulators designing emissions-reporting rules; standard-setter staff; researchers.
- **Useful if:** a user can tell which reductions are evidenced as real, through which mechanisms,
  and under which rule designs.

### S1.2 Focus
Map the mechanisms and factors underlying firms' greenhouse-gas emissions when emissions disclosure is
required, separating reductions in reported emissions from real ones.

### S1.3 Element space
- **Outcome:** a change in emissions (reported or real), or in a firm attribute that a reference
  links to emissions-disclosure requirements. Example: O-02 reported emissions.
- **Mechanism:** a firm or market process linking a requirement to an outcome. Example: M-01 peer
  benchmarking.
- **Factor:** a design feature of the requirement, or a firm or market condition, that changes whether
  or how much a mechanism operates. Example: F-05 consolidation-boundary rules.
- **Level of detail:** fine enough to separate reported from boundary-inclusive emissions, and to
  separate individual rule-design features.
- **Seeds:** taken from REF-0001 §1 and §3 (registry, S3.2).

### S1.4 Boundaries
| Excluded | Reason |
|---|---|
| Cost-of-capital, valuation and liquidity effects of emissions disclosure | Not emissions outcomes |
| Carbon pricing *without* a disclosure element | Different instrument. Included as Indirect only when the finding concerns a mechanism shared with disclosure (e.g. relocating assets to escape a rule) |
| Non-English references | Capacity; recorded as a limitation in S4.5 |

Included, although a user might not expect it: **evidence on emitting assets moving between owners**
(sales and relocations), even when not caused by a disclosure rule. Q3 cannot be answered without it.

### S1.5 Review questions
- **Q1** Do disclosure mandates reduce O-02, by how much, and in which contexts?
- **Q2** Which mechanisms are evidenced rather than only proposed?
- **Q3** Do reductions in O-02 correspond to reductions in O-03, or do firms redraw their boundaries?
- **Q4** Which factors (enforcement, sector, rule-design features F-04 to F-08) change Q1–Q3?
- **Q5** Where is evidence missing? Prioritise by relevance to the S1.1 design decisions.

---

## S2. Search

### S2.1 Sources
- **Seed and backward citation:** REF-0001 and the emissions studies it cites.
- **Academic databases:** OpenAlex, SSRN and RePEc.
- **Existing reviews and evidence maps** on climate-disclosure effects, used as ordinary references
  for citation chasing. Examples: literature reviews of mandatory sustainability reporting; living
  maps of climate-disclosure effectiveness.
- **Targeted searches** on asset divestment and regulatory arbitrage, for Q3.
- **Not searched (this version):** regulator compliance data and news.

### S2.2 Search procedure and log
- **OpenAlex queries:**
  - `("greenhouse gas reporting program" OR "carbon disclosure" OR "emissions disclosure" OR "GHG reporting") AND (mandat* OR regulat*) AND emission*`
  - `(divest* OR "plant sale*" OR "asset sale*" OR "regulatory arbitrage" OR leakage OR relocat*) AND (pollut* OR emission*) AND (firm* OR plant*)`
- **Citation chasing:** one backward round from the included CE references.
- **Log (`search_log`):** date, source, query or seed reference, number of results, number new after
  de-duplication.

### S2.3 Inclusion rules
| Rule | Passes | Fails |
|---|---|---|
| I1 Makes an empirical or theoretical claim involving firm or facility emissions | Study of facility emissions after a reporting mandate | Study of stock returns of high emitters with no emissions outcome |
| I2 The claim involves a disclosure requirement, **or** a mechanism this review tracks (M-01 to M-06) under another instrument | Plant divestment after environmental pressure | Study of carbon-tax incidence on households |
| I3 Full text or abstract accessible | SSRN working paper | No accessible version (logged as "unretrievable") |

Borderline cases go to the decision log.

### S2.4 Screening procedure
- **Stages:** title/abstract, then full text where accessible.
- **Double screening:** 20% of references are screened independently twice; report percentage agreement.
- **Disagreements:** resolved by discussion and logged.
- **Record per reference:** decision, rule that failed (if excluded), screener, date.

### S2.5 Updating
- **Schedule:** quarterly.
- **Event triggers:** a new emissions-reporting mandate; a revision of the GHG Protocol corporate
  standard.
- **Earlier decisions:** superseded with a reason, never overwritten.

---

## S3. Coding and appraisal

### S3.1 Unit of coding
- **One record = one claim** relating at least two elements, anchored to one passage.
- **Several findings in one reference:** one record each.
- **The same finding in several references:** coded from the most primary reference; other records
  point to it through `same_as`.
- **Second-hand reports:** coded with `primary_source` and `text_accessed = second_hand`. Once the
  primary is coded, the secondary record gets `superseded_by`.
- **Summary claims in reviews** (e.g. "reductions of 8–15%", REF-0001 p.12): not coded. The studies
  they summarise are added as search seeds.
- **Missing element roles:** if no mechanism is stated, the mechanism is left empty and the record is
  flagged `mechanism_unstated`.
- **Statements that evidence is lacking:** coded with evidence type `ABS`.

### S3.2 Element registry
| ID | Name | Definition | Broader | Status | added_in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O-01 | Firm GHG emissions | Emissions associated with firms subject to requirements | — | active | v0.1 |
| O-02 | Reported emissions | Emissions reported by, or measured for, covered entities | O-01 | active | v0.1 |
| O-03 | Boundary-inclusive emissions | Emissions including assets sold, outsourced or relocated outside the reporting boundary | O-01 | active | v0.1 |
| O-04 | Profitability | Operating performance of covered firms | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-01 | Peer benchmarking | Firms learn their relative performance from peers' disclosures | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-02 | Internal measurement | Being required to measure creates information inside the firm | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-03 | Outside monitoring | Investors, analysts and the public scrutinise disclosed emissions | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-04 | Investor engagement & divestment | Investors engage with emitters or exit them | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-05 | Boundary redrawing | Firms move emitting assets outside the reporting boundary (sale, outsourcing, relocation) | — | active | v0.1 |
| M-06 | Exemption use / avoidance | Firms use opt-outs or comply only in form | — | active | v0.1 |
| F-01 | Mandatory vs voluntary regime | Whether disclosure is required | — | active | v0.1 |
| F-02 | Enforcement & assurance | Supervision, sanctions and external assurance | — | active | v0.1 |
| F-03 | Sector carbon intensity | Emissions intensity of the firm's sector | — | active | v0.1 |
| F-04 | Standard discretion | Choices left to firms by the reporting rules | — | active | v0.1 |
| F-05 | Consolidation-boundary rules | Operational vs financial control and equity share (GHG Protocol) | F-04 | active | v0.1 |
| F-06 | Scope coverage | Which scopes (1/2/3) must be reported | F-04 | active | v0.1 |
| F-07 | Exemption clauses | Opt-out provisions in the requirement | F-04 | active | v0.1 |
| F-08 | Scrutiny gap between owners | Difference in disclosure pressure between the current owner and potential buyers (e.g. listed vs private) | — | active | v0.1 |

- **Add:** coders propose elements in the decision log; the review lead approves them and assigns the
  next ID.
- **Merge / split:** an element appearing in more than 5 records needs a change-log entry; otherwise
  the decision log is enough.

### S3.3 Coding schema
Core fields as in the template, plus:

| Field | Definition / values |
|---|---|
| `primary_source` | citation of the original study, if the record is second-hand |
| `same_as` / `superseded_by` | record IDs |
| `instrument` | named requirement or pressure, e.g. "US EPA GHG Reporting Program" |
| `direction` | `+` / `−` / `none` / `conditional` / `unclear` |
| `text_accessed` | `full_text` / `abstract` / `second_hand` |
| `emissions_measure` | `firm-reported` / `regulator-measured facility` / `provider-estimated` / `independent` / `not stated` |
| `boundary` | `facility` / `firm (as reported)` / `firm incl. divested assets` / `not stated` |
| `flags` | e.g. `mechanism_unstated` |

**Mechanism status (amended, see change log).** Each mechanism in `elements` carries `status`:
- `tested`: the reference reports evidence that bears specifically on this mechanism (e.g. a test of the channel, heterogeneity designed to isolate it, or a measured mediator);
- `proposed`: the reference offers it as an explanation, interpretation or hypothesis, without such evidence.

A record whose mechanisms are all `proposed` keeps its evidence type for the factor–outcome link, but the mechanism itself does not count as evidenced.

**Policy, place and time (amended, see change log).** Every record also carries:

| Field | Definition / values |
|---|---|
| `policies` | IDs from the policy list below (empty if no specific policy) |
| `jurisdictions` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, or `EU`, `multi` (list them in `context`) or `global` |
| `period` | `{start, end}`: years of the data or events studied. For a policy document, the year of the document |
| `evidence_year` | the year the finding first became public: the earliest known version of the primary study, or the year of a policy document |

**Policy list.** This table sits beside the element registry. Columns:
- `P-nn` ID;
- name;
- jurisdiction;
- type (`mandate` / `standard` / `voluntary framework` / `proposal`);
- key dates (proposed, adopted, effective, amended, withdrawn), each with a source;
- notes.

Entries are added and approved like elements (S3.2).

### S3.4 Appraisal
**Evidence type:**
- `CE`: causal estimate against a counterfactual;
- `AS`: association;
- `DE`: description;
- `TH`: theory;
- `EX`: expectation or conjecture;
- `ABS`: a statement that evidence is lacking.

**Strength** (CE and AS only):

| Level | Rule |
|---|---|
| High | CE addressing both selection into disclosure and concurrent changes |
| Medium | CE with one of those threats unaddressed, or a strong AS |
| Low | AS with obvious selection; or CE the reference itself says it cannot attribute |
| provisional | Second-hand or abstract-only |

**Relevance:**
- `Direct`: emissions-disclosure mandate, emissions outcome.
- `Indirect`: another instrument or pressure acting through a shared mechanism.
- `Remote`: anything further.

**Measurement** (review-specific dimension): can the outcome measure tell real reductions apart from
changes in reporting or boundary?

| Level | Rule |
|---|---|
| distinguishes | Independent or facility-level measure, with the boundary held fixed or tracked |
| partial | Firm-reported, but the boundary is held fixed |
| cannot | Firm-reported with a changing boundary, or pre-mandate values that are estimates |
| unknown | Not determinable from the text accessed |

### S3.5 Coding procedure and consistency
- **Coders:** one coder per reference; a second coder independently codes 20%.
- **Agreement:** element-set overlap (Jaccard) and κ for evidence type and strength.
- **Ambiguities logged:** any `direction = unclear`; any record whose effect on emissions depends on
  how an intermediate outcome is interpreted.

### S3.6 Worked examples
| Case | Record | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| CE, two outcomes from one passage | REC-001a/b: firms required to disclose reduced emissions relative to European controls (O-02, `−`), without affecting profitability (O-04, `none`) (REF-0001 p.11; Downar et al. 2021). Elements: F-01. CE, provisional, Direct. Measurement unknown | One passage → two records; a `none` result is coded |
| Indirect CE on boundary redrawing | REC-002: firms divest polluting plants in response to environmental pressure, to buyers facing weaker pressure; pollution at those plants does not decline (Duchin, Gao & Xu 2025). Elements: F-08, M-05, O-02 (`−`), O-03 (`none`). CE, Medium, Indirect, distinguishes | Unintended pathway; reported vs real outcome |
| Ambiguous direction (hard case) | REC-003: the UK rule lets firms not disclose by claiming it is "not practical"; information from required measurement "can discipline and lower CSR engagement" (REF-0001 p.11; De Bettignies et al. 2020). Elements: F-07, M-06, M-02. `direction = unclear`. Logged | Decision-log routing |
| Out of scope | Newly disclosing high emitters faced a higher cost of capital (REF-0001 p.12). Excluded under S1.4 (not an emissions outcome); logged | Boundary rule applied at record level |

---

## S4. Synthesis

### S4.1 Outputs
1. **Summary by question** (Q1–Q5).
2. **Table: reported vs real:** each O-02 statement is paired with the O-03 evidence, or with the
   absence of it.
3. **Gap list.**

### S4.2 From records to statements
- **Grouping:** by outcome, then mechanism, then factor.
- **Conflicts:** conditional statements where `context` explains the conflict; otherwise labelled
  *inconsistent*.
- **Citing:** every statement lists its record IDs and the `measurement` level of each. A statement
  whose records are all `cannot` is not written as a claim about real emissions.

### S4.3 Confidence
| Level | Rule |
|---|---|
| High | ≥2 independent High/Direct records, agreeing |
| Moderate | ≥1 High, or ≥2 Medium, agreeing |
| Low | Only Low or provisional records, or only Indirect relevance |
| Expected only | Only TH/EX records |

**Added rule:** a statement about O-03 cannot be rated above Low unless at least one record has
`measurement = distinguishes`.

### S4.4 Gaps
**Gap types:**
- (a) an outcome with no CE/AS records;
- (b) a mechanism with only TH/EX records;
- (c) a context in scope with no records;
- (d) any ABS record;
- (e) a mechanism evidenced for O-02 but never tested against O-03.

**Priority:** gaps that bear on F-05, F-06 and F-07 (rule design) come first.

**Added gap type (f) (amended, see change log):** *untested mechanism*. A mechanism whose records all have `status = proposed`.

### S4.5 Interpretation and limits
- **Not made:** no policy recommendations.
- **Standing limitations:**
  - English only;
  - early versions rely heavily on second-hand and abstract-only records;
  - the seed note may shape the element set.

### S4.6 Versions of the synthesis
- **When:** quarterly, if any statement or gap changes.
- **Change table:** statements added, revised or retired, each with its cause.

**Synthesis history (amended, see change log).** Every statement and gap keeps a `history`: its records ordered by `evidence_year`. For each record:
- `effect`: one of `establishes` / `corroborates` / `extends` (new context) / `qualifies` (adds a condition) / `contradicts` / `weakens` / `signals_gap`;
- a one-sentence blurb on how the record changed the statement relative to earlier records.

The synthesis from the previous release is kept, so changes between releases can be shown.

---

## S5. Maintenance

### S5.1 Decision log
`decision_log` with the template's minimum fields. Reviewed at each release; any ambiguity logged
three or more times triggers a proposed change.

### S5.2 Change log
| Change ID | Date | Item ID | Change | Reason | Effect on existing records | Version after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CH-001 | 2026-11-24 | S3.3 | Mechanism entries have no status → each mechanism carries `status`: tested / proposed | Pilot: Q2 asks which mechanisms are proposed vs evidenced, but the schema could not record it (run notes and decision log); user request | recode all records | 0.2 |
| CH-002 | 2026-11-24 | S3.3 | No structured policy/place/time → add `policies`, `jurisdictions`, `period`, `evidence_year`, plus a policy list | Context was free text, so records could not be related to specific policies, countries or periods; user request | recode all records | 0.3 |
| CH-003 | 2026-11-24 | S4.4 | Gap types → add (f) untested mechanism | Follows from the mechanism-status change; pilot found mechanisms supported only by explanations | none (regenerate gaps) | 0.4 |
| CH-004 | 2026-11-24 | S4.6 | No per-statement provenance over time → statements and gaps keep a `history` of records with effect and blurb | Needed to show how the synthesis built up over time; user request | none (regenerate synthesis) | 0.5 |

review.title: Does enforcement make disclosure work? How enforcement, assurance and institutions shape what mandates achieve
review.focus: Map the outcomes and mechanisms through which enforcement, assurance and broader institutional quality change what mandatory corporate disclosure achieves.

questions.text: How do the outcomes of disclosure mandates differ with the strength of enforcement, assurance and the regulatory channel?
Through which mechanisms does enforcement act?
Do common standards make reporting practice converge or diverge across institutional settings?
What evidence exists for emerging and developing economies?
Where is evidence missing? Prioritise by relevance to the S1.1 adoption decisions.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: In financial reporting, capital-market benefits of mandatory IFRS adoption are concentrated where enforcement changed at the same time or legal enforcement is strong; averaged across countries, and in strong-legal-system countries without enforcement change, liquidity effects are small or absent, while enforcement changes without IFRS show similar liquidity effects.
statements.confidence_reason: All records are CE but abstract-only (strength provisional) and all are Indirect; S4.3 'Low: only Low or provisional records, or only Indirect relevance' applies on both counts.
statements.conditions: Transfer conditions: Financial statements are audited under mature, mandatory audit regimes with established supervisors (e.g. national enforcers); climate data rely on less mature assurance (often limited assurance, mixed providers) and supervisors with little track record, and climate metrics are more judgemental, so enforcement effects may be weaker or slower. Securities-regulation evidence (REF-0005) relies on established national supervisors that climate disclosure lacks.

history.blurb: First cross-country evidence (26 countries, 2001-2005) that IFRS capital-market benefits arise only where legal enforcement is strong and firms have transparency incentives.
Carries the enforcement condition to EU securities regulation (MAD/TPD): liquidity gains are larger with stricter implementation and stronger prior regulation.
Shows the average liquidity effect of mandatory IFRS across all adopters is small, so the benefit is not a general property of the mandate.
Locates the IFRS liquidity effect in five EU countries with concurrent enforcement changes, sharpening the condition from strong legal enforcement to enforcement change.
Strong legal systems without an enforcement change show no liquidity benefit, so the REC-011 condition is necessary but not sufficient.
Similar liquidity effects from enforcement changes without IFRS support enforcement, rather than the standards, as the driver.

statements.question: Q1
statements.text: ESG disclosure mandates raise stock liquidity, and the effect is strongest where the mandate is issued by a government body, is not comply-or-explain, and is backed by strong informal enforcement.
statements.confidence_reason: One reference, abstract-only (provisional) CE records; Direct. S4.3: only provisional records -> Low.
statements.conditions: Multi-country ESG mandates; country composition not verified from the abstract. Mechanism for the channel/informal-enforcement contrast not stated.

history.blurb: First Direct causal evidence that ESG disclosure mandates raise stock liquidity (25 countries, 2000-2017).
Same study: the effect is strongest for government-issued, not comply-or-explain mandates with strong informal enforcement.

statements.question: Q1

Same study: the effects are larger with stronger law enforcement and more widespread assurance.

Confirms the rule-of-law condition in this independent sample and adds that effects are larger where stakeholders engage less.

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: PROPOSED only (M-03 sanction credibility): no coded record tests sanction credibility as the channel through which supervision acts on sustainability reporting. Theory and expectation propose that subjective CSR metrics and materiality judgements make noncompliance hard to detect and sanction.
statements.confidence_reason: Only TH/EX records, and every M-03 mention has status 'proposed'.

history.blurb: Proposes that subjective CSR metrics make noncompliance hard for regulators and courts to identify, weakening sanction credibility (theory).
The seed note restates the expectation and points to materiality judgements; still proposed only.

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: TESTED mechanism (M-02 incentive-driven use of discretion), financial-reporting analogue only: capital-market benefits around IAS/IFRS adoption accrue to 'serious' adopters, classified by firm-level changes in reporting incentives and actual reporting behaviour, and not to 'label' adopters. Results are similar around mandatory adoption.
statements.confidence_reason: Single provisional AS record (abstract-only), Indirect. S4.3 -> Low.
statements.conditions: Transfer conditions: Financial statements are audited under mature, mandatory audit regimes with established supervisors (e.g. national enforcers); climate data rely on less mature assurance (often limited assurance, mixed providers) and supervisors with little track record, and climate metrics are more judgemental, so enforcement effects may be weaker or slower. Incentive heterogeneity is likely larger for climate disclosure.

history.blurb: Tests incentive-driven use of discretion through a 'serious' vs 'label' split built from measured firm-level changes in incentives and reporting behaviour.

statements.question: Q2
statements.text: For most enforcement, assurance and institutional contrasts, the coded studies do not state a mechanism (mechanism_unstated): this includes the enforcement-change liquidity results, the regulatory-channel and informal-enforcement results, and the rule-of-law and assurance contrasts for real outcomes.
statements.confidence_reason: Statement about the evidence base built from records flagged mechanism_unstated, all provisional. Confidence rule S4.3 applied to the underlying records -> Low.
statements.conditions: Partly Indirect (IFRS and EU securities regulation): Transfer conditions: Financial statements are audited under mature, mandatory audit regimes with established supervisors (e.g. national enforcers); climate data rely on less mature assurance (often limited assurance, mixed providers) and supervisors with little track record, and climate metrics are more judgemental, so enforcement effects may be weaker or slower.

history.blurb: Earliest coded institutional contrast (legal systems and earnings management) with no stated mechanism.
Implementation and enforcement contrasts for EU securities regulation are reported without a mechanism.
The IFRS enforcement-change result names no channel.
Enforcement-only liquidity effects are attributed to enforcement 'or (unobserved) factors associated with these changes', with no channel.
The pattern extends to real sustainability outcomes: the enforcement and assurance moderation is reported without a channel.
The pattern extends to Direct ESG mandates: the regulatory-channel and informal-enforcement contrasts are reported without a channel.
The rule-of-law moderation of mandate announcements is reported without a channel.

statements.question: Q3
statements.text: Common standards are not expected to make reporting practice converge where firms' incentives and institutions differ; enforcement only partly narrows the variation, and differences between developed and developing economies may produce less convergence. The one empirical analogue (EU securities regulation) found that capital-market outcomes diverged further after harmonisation.
statements.confidence_reason: Mostly TH/EX; one provisional, Indirect CE record (on liquidity divergence, not reporting practice). With one empirical record S4.3 'Expected only' does not strictly apply; 'Low' applied.
statements.conditions: Transfer conditions: REC on EU securities regulation measures divergence in liquidity (O-01), not in reporting practice (O-03); the developed-developing gap may be larger than within the EU.

history.blurb: Earliest record and only empirical one: harmonised EU securities regulation widened liquidity gaps (divergence in outcomes, not reporting practice).
Proposes that convergence of practice requires similar incentives, which is rare.
Enforcement narrows but cannot remove incentive-driven variation.
Enforcement cannot reach discretion deliberately built into standards.
The seed note restates that standards alone will not make practice converge without harmonised institutions.
Applies the argument to developed vs developing economies and expects possibly less convergence.

statements.question: Q4
statements.text: No coded record isolates emerging or developing economies. Two multi-country studies include emerging economies but do not report them separately. In mandatory sustainability reporting laws (incl. China, Malaysia and South Africa), effects are larger with stronger law enforcement and assurance. In ESG disclosure mandates across 25 countries (incl. China and South Africa), liquidity effects are strongest with government implementation and strong informal enforcement. Climate standards are expected to have very different effects in developed and developing economies, and to have small effects where the institutional ecosystem is underdeveloped.
statements.confidence_reason: The developed-vs-developing claim rests only on EX records. The mixed-sample records (provisional AS/CE) do not report emerging-economy results separately, so they support the enforcement contrast in general, not Q4 specifically.
statements.conditions: Mixed samples: REF-0060 MCSR countries per its SSRN abstract; REF-0008 country examples from the authors' 2021 summary of the working paper (published-version sample not checked).

history.blurb: First empirical record with emerging economies in its sample (MCSR laws incl. China, Malaysia, South Africa); results not reported separately.
Same study: effects larger with stronger law enforcement and assurance, which bears on weaker-institution adopters only indirectly.
Newly identified through jurisdiction coding (CH-002): the ESG-mandate liquidity sample includes China and South Africa, but results are not separated.
Same study: effects strongest with government implementation and strong informal enforcement; no emerging-economy split in the abstract.
Introduces the expectation that effects differ sharply between developed and developing economies.
Expects standards to matter little where the institutional ecosystem is underdeveloped.

statements.question: Q5
statements.text: Authors flag missing evidence: IFRS studies cannot separate the effect of new standards from bundled enforcement changes; causal evidence on disclosure regulation is still rare; and whether and how enforcement improves the effectiveness of CSR standards is an open research question.
statements.confidence_reason: ABS records (plus one EX). S4.3 has no rule for ABS-only statements; 'Low' assigned by default (see decision log and proposed change CH-P04).
statements.conditions: Partly Indirect: Transfer conditions: the bundling problem will recur if climate standards are introduced with new supervision/assurance at the same time.

history.blurb: The authors themselves flag that concurrent enforcement and governance reforms may drive the IFRS effects.
A major review states that causal evidence on disclosure regulation is still rare.
Second-hand: the same review concludes that bundling IFRS with stricter enforcement prevents separating the two effects.
Names whether and how enforcement improves CSR standards as an open question (2021 wording).

statements.question: Q2

Enforcement cannot constrain discretion that standards deliberately allow, so practice will not converge where incentives and institutions differ, including between developed and developing economies. No Direct record tests this; the only test of M-02 is the IFRS analogue (ST-11).
statements.confidence_reason: Only TH/EX records, all with mechanism status 'proposed'.
